summary: Iteration 1: backend 27/27 pytest pass (demo auth, 401 guards, me/onboarding validation, watchlist CRUD+validation+owner 404s, barcode lookup, live Exa deal check, deals/savings/alerts). Frontend (390x844 web preview) all requested flows work: sign-in, Explore the demo -> Deals masonry with store chips + filtering, Check deals now loading -> in-app banner, Watchlist add/edit/delete via FAB/modal, Savings total + per-store breakdown, Profile edit stores (onboarding?edit=1, 4-store cap, continue disabled <2 stores / bad ZIP, returns to profile), scan permission screen -> type instead, Exit demo -> sign-in (persists across reload). Main problems are deal-quality and data consistency: the live Exa scoring produces false-positive deals (prices taken from other products), deals from removed stores remain, and Deals header total does not match Savings total. No deprecated Expo packages found (expo-camera, expo-notifications used).

critical.issue: False-positive deals from keyword windows on generic words. Seen live: 'Large Eggs' $1.99 at Kroger from a snippet about 'Pepperidge Goldfish Crackers ... $1.99 / Kellogg's Large Size Cereal' (matched 'large'); 'Ground Coffee' $5.99 from 'Kroger 80% Lean Ground Beef $5.99' (matched 'ground'); 'Boneless Chicken Breast' $7.99 from 'Boneless Chuck Roast'; 'Cheerios' BOGO at Kroger with only a generic 'cereal ... clip digital' snippet; Walmart Tide $6.97 'cashback' from generic article text. This inflates savings ($23.06) and alerts users with wrong deals. Fix: require the full item name (or most of its tokens, and brand when given) inside the window, use a stopword list for generic words (large, ground, boneless, whole, organic, ...), and only take prices close to the matched phrase.

minor.issue: When stores change, existing deals (live + is_sample) for removed stores are kept. Verified: after switching to Kroger+Aldi, Deals 'All' still showed Walmart/Target cards and Savings still counted them. Delete deals for stores not in the new list, or filter GET /deals and /savings by user.stores.
Sample deals (is_sample) stay next to live deals for the same item/store (e.g., Kroger Large Eggs sample $3.49 and live $1.99). Think about clearing samples after the first real check.
Returns 500 because EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY is 'placeholder' in backend/.env. This is expected in preview, but native push registration will fail until a real key is set.
Every demo session shares the single demo_user document, so any visitor's edits (watchlist, stores) show up for all demo visitors.

integration_issues.issue: Deals header 'deals-total-savings' adds up every deal row, including duplicates for the same item across stores and samples, giving $39.50. Savings uses the best deal per item and shows $23.06. The two numbers on one screen pair contradict each other. Use the same per-item-best logic, or label it differently.

issues: The 'On sale' pill wraps to 2 lines ('On / sale') next to long item names (Laundry Detergent Pacs, Boneless Chicken). Add numberOfLines={1}/flexShrink:0 to the pill.
Trash icon hit area is 28x28 (hitSlop 8 helps on native). The visual target is under 44pt.
The usual-price TextInput shows the browser's black focus outline, which overflows the rounded price container on web. Set outlineStyle:'none' on web.
Store tiles expose no accessibilityState selected/checked (aria-selected null), which is an a11y gap.
useEffect resets zip/stores whenever me.data refetches (e.g., window refocus), which can wipe in-progress edits.
Deal card promo_text shows raw mid-word Exa snippets (e.g., 'epperidge Goldfish...', 'cy here. Walmart has...'), which looks broken. Trim to word boundaries.

action_items: HIGH: Tighten score_result/_relevant in server.py so deals match the actual product (full name/brand tokens, generic-word stopwords, prices next to the phrase). Current live results attach other products' prices to watchlist items.
Remove or filter deals for stores the user deselected in PUT /api/me/onboarding (or filter /deals and /savings by user.stores).
Make the Deals header total match the Savings total (best deal per item), or relabel it.
Fix the 'On sale' pill wrapping in watchlist.tsx and enlarge the trash touch target to 44pt.
Trim Exa promo_text snippets to word boundaries.
Optional: per-visitor demo users. Set a real EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY for native push.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py score_result: keywords = 4+ letter words from the name only (brand ignored), so 'large', 'ground', 'boneless' match unrelated products. _relevant also passes on any 3+ letter word from name or brand.
server.py run_check: the BOGO fallback sets sale=usual/2 whenever 'buy' appears in the window, even with no evidence the item itself is BOGO.
server.py daily_check: users are processed one after another with up to 25 Exa calls each. Fine for now, but it won't scale.
Uses deprecated @app.on_event startup/shutdown. Consider a lifespan handler.
onboarding.tsx edit mode uses router.back(). If /onboarding?edit=1 is opened directly (web refresh), there is no history to go back to.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% of requested flows pass; issues are data consistency and design

seed_data_creation: None. TEST_ watchlist items were created and deleted. Demo stores were temporarily changed and restored to 75201 / Kroger, Walmart, Target. Demo watchlist is back to the 6 seeded items.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_promobeaux_api.py (pytest.ini enables xdist; use -n 0 to see prints). Writing files under /app/backend triggers a uvicorn reload. The live Exa check finished in about 0.5s and returned checked=6, found=7. Verify the deal relevance fix by inspecting the promo_text of each non-sample deal from GET /api/deals.
rca_of_issue: False deals: score_result builds windows around any 4+ letter token of item.name, then picks the minimum $ price in the 40-95% range of usual_price inside those windows. Weekly-ad roundup pages list many products, so generic tokens land next to other products' prices. Stale store deals: PUT /me/onboarding updates the user only and never touches the deals collection.
